memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "but the Israelites were exceedingly fruitful; they multiplied greatly, increased in numbers and became so numerous that the land was filled with them." - Exodus 1:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Four hundred years pass between the last chapter of Genesis and this verse. Four hundred silent years — no recorded prophet, no dramatic miracle, no voice from heaven. And yet look what God was doing all that time: seventy people quietly became a nation.

This verse deliberately echoes God's very first command to humanity, to be fruitful and increase (Gen 1:28), and His promise to Abraham that his descendants would be countless. God had not forgotten. He was simply working in silence.

We tend to measure God's activity by how much we can feel or see. But some of the deepest work God does in us is slow and hidden — in the years of an unnoticed job, an unanswered prayer, a long illness, a delayed marriage. Growth underground is still growth.

If God can keep a promise across four centuries of silence, He can be trusted with the silence in your life right now. The same patient faithfulness eventually brought forth Christ Himself, born in the fullness of time (Gal 4:4).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I mistaking God's silence for God's absence?
2. What has God been quietly growing in me over these years?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, when I hear nothing from You, help me to remember that You are still at work. Grow me quietly and keep me trusting. Amen.
